headlines.text: 2020 brought us this moment: it was title-change night for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Kenny Omega vs. Jon Moxley battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.87 ? a solid showing ? ending the champion's reign at 9 defenses. Jon Moxley was chasing gold for the 10th time. A shocking title change on AEW's inaugural "Winter Is Coming" special ? Omega ended Moxley's nine-month reign with outside interference from Don Callis, before the two fled the building together in a wild, controversial swerve that set up a surprise Impact Wrestling crossover angle.

That Saturday in 2023, Bryan Danielson vs. Eddie Kingston met in a Continental Classic League Match, topping the bill that night on Collision, rated 8.47 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. In their first-ever singles meeting, Danielson used a strap-assisted LeBell Lock to force Kingston to submit in the opening round of the Continental Classic.

Turning the clock back to 2022: the AEW All-Atlantic Title was up for grabs as Orange Cassidy vs. QT Marshall went to war in a Lumberjack match, appearing on Rampage, rated 5.50. For QT Marshall, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. It was the 10th time the AEW All-Atlantic Title had been on the line, a notable milestone for the title. Championship gold always raises the stakes.

secondaries.text: Turning the clock back to 2020: Will Hobbs left that name behind for good, stepping out as Powerhouse Hobbs after 2 matches under the old identity, on Dynamite.

Looking back to 2020, when Lee Johnson laced up for their first AEW match in a Battle Royal match against MJF vs. Orange Cassidy vs. Adam Page vs. Alex Reynolds vs. Isiah Kassidy vs. Joey Janela vs. John Silver vs. Jungle Boy vs. Kip Sabian vs. Luther vs. Marq Quen vs. Matt Hardy vs. Matt Sydal vs. Miro vs. Sammy Guevara vs. Scorpio Sky vs. Serpentico vs. Shawn Spears vs. Wardlow, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.33.
That Saturday in 2023, Christopher Daniels returned to the fold after 7 weeks away, appearing on Collision.
